![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14111253/assets/9a66f9263c9009f634668e826f0a84320103589b9c270360d7b2465c71e74592.png)

Evaluate the triple integral 
${∭}_{R}2xz\,dV$
over the region $R,$ shown above.

*Hint: All surfaces, except for the top one, are parallel to the corresponding coordinate planes.*
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14111253/assets/49a3333a52a6b7d7451095dbc46ab1009df491c92726436929a6f93cff38db60.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written as the type I region

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,\,0\le z\le 3-2x},
$$

where

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le 2}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane, shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14111253/assets/dfa0a80bc323401f050d1302dc42c92558d8b566d9b0f985e955d34eb5cc15bd.png)

Hence, we can express the region $R$ as

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 3-2x}
$$

As a result, by writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}2xz\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3-2x}2xz\,dz\,dy\,dx.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z$, treating $x$ and $y$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3-2x}2xz\,dz\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{3-2x}2xz\,dz]dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}[x{z}^{2}]_{z=0}^{z=3-2x}\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}x(3-2x)^{2}\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}(9x-12{x}^{2}+4{x}^{3})\,dy\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}(9x-12{x}^{2}+4{x}^{3})\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{2}(9x-12{x}^{2}+4{x}^{3})\,dy]dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(9x-12{x}^{2}+4{x}^{3}){[y]}_{y=0}^{y=2}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2(9x-12{x}^{2}+4{x}^{3})\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(18x-24{x}^{2}+8{x}^{3})\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}(18x-24{x}^{2}+8{x}^{3})\,dx & ={[9{x}^{2}-8{x}^{3}+2{x}^{4}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =[9-8+2] \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
